Maladaptive Strategies.value: I dwell on what I have done wrong
deliberately try to leave my body or blank out
ruminate about how event could have been prevented

Threat.value: Even when others tell me I am safe I find it impossible to believe it
When something takes longer than expected I assume something bad is happening
I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place

Memory.value: I can taste what I tasted during the event when the memory returns
When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.
The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me

Negative Appraisals.value: The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am
The world is a dangerous place
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.item: Triggers: Victim Similarity: People who look similar to the victims
issues.explanation: For a mugging/robbery trauma, 'people who look similar to the victims' is clinically incoherent because the patient is the victim; a plausible trigger would be people resembling the perpetrator(s) or contextual robbery cues. As written, this item conflicts with the trauma type.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Contamination: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened
issues.explanation: Feeling dirty/contaminated is not impossible after robbery, but in this profile it is hard to reconcile with the rest of the selected items, which otherwise center on danger, self-blame, and moral injury rather than sexual violation or disgust-based trauma themes. This makes the appraisal set clinically inconsistent with the trauma context.

For a mugging/robbery trauma, 'Being naked' as a primary trigger is hard to reconcile unless there was a stripping/sexual humiliation element, which is not suggested elsewhere in the profile. The other trigger items point to perpetrator proximity and assault cues, making this vulnerability trigger clinically incongruent with the stated trauma type.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Violated Values: I acted in ways that go against who I am
issues.explanation: 'I acted in ways that go against who I am' implies morally troubling behaviour during the event, but the rest of the profile reflects victim-focused danger, self-blame, and mistrust rather than any specific morally injurious action. In a mugging/robbery context this item is difficult to justify without corroborating memory/appraisal content about the patient's own behaviour.

vignette: Leilani had been walking to her car in the dimly lit garage of her downtown office building, the damp air heavy with exhaust and the metallic tang of the city. A set of heavy footsteps had echoed from the stairwell, closing in on her pace. Before she could turn, a hand had clamped onto her shoulder, yanking her backward into a concrete pillar. A man's face, marked by a jagged scar across his jaw, had filled her vision as he demanded her wallet. She had fought, freezing, tasting the sharp, bitter dregs of the coffee she'd finished just before leaving her desk. The struggle was brief, violent, and left her shaken but unharmed except for a bruised shoulder and a terror that lodged deep in her chest. In the weeks that followed, Leilani's life contracted. What frightened her most was not the act itself, but the sudden betrayal of a quiet night. She began to map every walk, every commute, avoiding the garage entirely by taking longer routes through well-lit commercial strips. At home, she waited at the window until her husband returned from his shift, certain that if he did not walk through the door within thirty minutes of his usual time, something terrible had already occurred. When her husband would reach around to hug her from behind, she would flinch, her muscles locking into the exact hunched posture she'd held against the pillar. She tried to push the memory away by deliberately blanking out, trying to lift herself out of her own body, but the taste of that bitter coffee would surge back, so vivid she could feel the acidity on her tongue. She told herself the event was too violent to be real, that it must have been a nightmare or a hallucination, yet her knees would buckle and her body would tremble in the living room where she stood. She had come to believe that the violence was a reflection of her own character, that the universe had targeted her because of something inherent in who she was, and that the world outside was fundamentally hostile. As an accountant, her days became a series of guarded routines. She requested a corner desk away from the main corridor, refusing to take the late audit shifts that required evening walks. When a colleague clapped her on the back to congratulate her on a completed reconciliation, she stepped back instantly, her breath catching. In her office, the loading times for financial reports became a source of quiet panic; if a spreadsheet took more than a few seconds to render, she was convinced she had missed a critical alert or that a crisis was unfolding elsewhere. She paced her cubicle, running through every possible mistake she might have made, every step she could have taken to avoid the mugging, convinced that if she had simply walked faster, worn a different coat, or stayed home, the man with the scar would never have found her. Even when her husband reminded her that the neighborhood had improved, that locks were changed, that she was secure now, Leilani found it impossible to absorb the words. Her body refused to settle, her shoulders perpetually drawn tight, her mind scanning the periphery of every room. The silence between tasks felt heavy, charged with an unspoken warning. The tipping point came during a family dinner when she missed her sister's laughter because she was staring at the shadow cast by a passing car's headlights on the dining room wall. She knew she could not keep rebuilding her life around narrow corridors and delayed loading screens while her body waited for the next strike. She sat down with a clinic referral, hoping to find a way to stop the blank-outs and stop waiting at windows, most of all hoping to believe that a quiet night could finally be just a quiet night. She was terrified that the world would always feel like a threat, but she desperately wanted to reclaim the life she had carved out before the garage, the coffee, and the footsteps.
